finding.claim: The /rss endpoint opens an arbitrary user-supplied URL with open-uri and returns the first 400 bytes of the response. An attacker can reach internal services or cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) and read the response. open-uri follows redirects, including http to https. Severity: HIGH, with no authentication and a response returned to the caller.

trace.note: get "/rss" handler receives the unauthenticated request
params[:u] is passed directly to URI.open (open-uri), which fetches it and the body is read
the first 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, no host allowlist, and no IP or CIDR filtering between source and sink. The TRUSTED allowlist at line 5 is not applied on this route. No authentication or before filter exists in the file. open-uri follows redirects by default, so there is no redirect restriction either.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes params[:u] straight to URI.open(...).read and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes. The only host allowlist (TRUSTED, app.rb:5, checked at app.rb:14) applies to the separate /trusted route, and app.rb has no auth or before filter.
